title: Make with AI on My Cuff or Bag
sentence: Arrange materials, photograph your composition, and let AI combine it with a textile source. Rearrange and compare the next response.
rq: How do people maintain or revise their understandings of authenticity through interaction with AI and cultural heritage?
purpose: A explores how people maintain or change their understanding of authenticity while making with AI and a named textile source. People express an interpretation by assembling ordinary materials. A cuff or bag provides an everyday setting for the digital result.
steps: Look at the textile source
Read the named object’s image and checked background. Choose a detail you want to work with.
Make your own arrangement
Place, overlap, join or fold ordinary fabric, paper strips and shapes on a small tabletop mat. Use the arrangement to express something you see or understand in the textile.
Photograph the arrangement
Check the camera preview and approve a photograph of your composition. This photograph is the input that carries your material choices to AI.
See AI combine both inputs

AI uses the named textile reference and your approved arrangement photograph to propose an adaptation. View it on a cuff or bag image. Keep the source, arrangement photo and AI result visible together.
Rearrange and get another response

Move, separate, overlap or fold the materials after seeing the result. Approve a new photograph. AI uses the same source and this new input to produce the next version. Compare the two results, or keep the first.
Explain and keep a result
Point to what connects the result to the textile and what carries your own interpretation. Discuss the proposed future museum label and keep a source-credited visual record.
ai: AI is a visual partner responding to a person’s material composition. It combines two inputs: the named textile reference and an approved photograph of the person’s arrangement. Rearranging and photographing again guides the next response. The digital cuff or bag is a presentation setting for that response.
noai: People can explore the source and make a material composition without generation, then keep a source-labelled record. Round 1 separately allows skipping activities and discarding drafts under its submitted protocol.
theory: Relational authenticity asks how a connection becomes meaningful through objects, people, making and history. We follow the connections visitors themselves describe.
Looking alike and having a real link
A similar shape is one possible reason. A known maker, source or history gives another kind of link. The personal item and original work each retain their own materials and histories.

Follow how a person expresses an interpretation with materials, sees how AI handles it and changes the next input. Ask how they judge the resulting connection to the textile. Art Morph and embodied-generation studies provide close interaction precedents.
future: Imagine a museum that lets visitors assemble materials and use AI to carry a textile work into everyday patterns. Its label says “Each version continues the original work”. Looking at your arrangement and the two previews, what would you keep, change or rename in that museum?
speculation: The two actual previews and the clearly fictional label make this future museum concrete. Visitors can discuss how personal use carries a source forward, what should remain recognisable and how the artist and source should be credited. Their own answer guides the discussion.
record: For a later study of the full interaction, a proposed record could link the source, approved arrangement photographs, actual AI outputs, material changes and participant explanations. That later protocol would specify collection and storage. Round 1 retains the separate anonymous data listed below.
analysis: Follow how a person’s arrangement, AI’s interpretation and the next material change affect what they see as connected to the source. Round 1 gathers questionnaire reflections, optional captions and source/image choices to refine this activity.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how visitors maintain or change their grounds for a connection to one named heritage object during material interaction with AI. The interaction technique has close precedents. A contribution would need evidence from the action sequence and the visitor’s reasons.
setup: A permitted textile reference and fact card, ordinary fabric and paper pieces, a small tabletop mat, a fixed camera and one screen with an image-generation service. A prepared cuff or bag image can provide the output setting. Photograph the arrangement itself. A personal-item photograph is an optional later input choice.
broad: Offer seated access, large easy-to-handle pieces, prepared outlines and a helper who follows the participant’s directions. People can arrange, point or describe a placement. A prepared everyday-item image supports participation without using a personal item.
checkpoint: Use Round 1 feedback to refine the task, examples and research prompts. Later iterations can test the live action-and-response loop and choose a detailed study method.

title: One Object, Two Interpretations
sentence: Exchange interpretations of the same object across languages, clarify the meaning, and develop a postcard that carries the exchange forward.
rq: How do people express and negotiate their understanding of a shared heritage object through AI-mediated cross-cultural exchange?
purpose: B explores expression, understanding and negotiation around one shared heritage object. People contribute interpretations, receive real replies and clarify meaning with AI language and image assistance. A related postcard develops from the conversation. The exchange can use a digital interface or paper notes with a small AI screen.
steps: Share one named object
Use the same named object image, selected detail and checked information. Display them on a screen or on a physical board.
Express an interpretation
Write or say what the object means to you in your own language. Use a message field or a paper note. Check the original words before any AI assistance.
Develop and share a draft
AI assists with a translation and a source-related image preview. Check the wording and image. Keep original words and labelled assistance together on screen or on adjacent paper notes.
Receive a real response

Another person reads the source and your interpretation, then replies or asks a question. They may use the interface or add a connected paper note. Different cultural perspectives can meet in one place.
Clarify and update

Keep the conversation visible. Clarify your meaning after the reply and, when useful, revise the associated image. Select your own message to connect the exchange to a postcard. Different interpretations can remain.
Keep a connected postcard

Keep a visual postcard linked to the source and your selected message. Later implementation options include a digital copy and a printed postcard. A printer is a possible future addition. Delivery arrangements will be specified for that stage.
ai: AI bridges languages and helps visualise an interpretation. People check suggested translations and images, receive a real human reply and clarify their meaning. This role can work through a digital interface or a small screen beside a physical conversation board.
noai: Use direct language skills or study-team translation and a plain postcard showing the source, local-item reference and checked words. The real reply and clarification still develop that same card. Choose translation, image generation and delivery separately.
theory: Follow how the object, a person’s experience and the other visitor become connected through exchange.
Separate the sender’s endorsement of wording, the recipient’s understanding, historical accuracy and the recognition of an interpretation.

Being able to change a translation can help people express themselves. It can also make a conversation take more effort. AI writing suggestions may remove cultural details. These findings help us choose what to observe.
future: Imagine a future museum that shows the final AI-assisted postcards as visitors’ interpretations of an object. Which parts of your developing card should the next visitor see: the final version, the earlier draft and reply, or both?
speculation: Use the actual draft, real reply and final card beside a fictional future-display label. Participants decide how a museum should show a meaning that developed through conversation, and whose words or images should remain visible. The real source and each contributor remain identified.
record: A later working-prototype study could link original messages, translations, real replies, clarifications and related postcard versions. Approved local photographs and delivery choices would need their own specified handling. Round 1 collects the anonymous text and existing-image references listed in its protocol.
analysis: The working concept asks how meanings travel through expression, AI assistance, another person’s reply and clarification. Round 1 uses original messages, reply relationships, related postcards and questionnaire reflections to refine that activity.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how a source-related personal meaning develops through a multilingual conversation around one AI-assisted visual postcard. Its draft and revision show how people recognise, question and clarify each other’s interpretations. The final card keeps the outcome of that same process.
setup: Two implementation options share the same interaction: a digital conversation interface, or a physical board with paper messages and a small AI-assistance screen. In the hybrid option, the participant or facilitator enters the chosen words for AI, the participant checks the result, and the original note stays visible. A cuff/bag image can be an optional visual setting. A printer may be added in a later version.
broad: Offer paper or digital expression, different languages, help with input and participation without a personal device. People can respond to an earlier contribution or a person present. A later digital version can retain a paper entry route.
checkpoint: Use Round 1 to improve the conversation and postcard relationship. Later iterations can test live language and image assistance and specify the study procedure.
